rules.description: Questions must align with NCERT/CBSE syllabus and prescribed grade level. Reject if outdated or outside rationalized 2025–26 content.
Questions must match Bloom’s levels: Factual (Easy), Understanding (Easy/Medium/Hard), Application (Medium/Hard). Reject if too simplistic.
Questions should be grammatically correct, unambiguous, and clearly worded. Reject if vague or confusing.
Questions must provide all necessary context or data. Reject if incomplete or assumes unstated knowledge.
Ensure facts, terminology, and figures are accurate. Reject if factually incorrect.
Avoid repeating similar questions. Reject minimal variations or format-only changes.
Questions must be neutral and inclusive. Reject if biased (gender, religious, political, regional, etc.).
Must be based on the NCERT curriculum and appropriate content cell. Use 10–15 words, grade-level vocabulary.
SCQs must be tagged accurately by Bloom’s taxonomy and difficulty level (Easy/Medium/Hard).
One correct answer, three plausible distractors based on common misconceptions. Reject if options are irrelevant.
Start with 'The correct answer is...'. Justify correct answer and incorrect ones clearly and briefly.
Ensure the provided solution matches the correct option.
Assertion/Reason logic must be clear. Use standard options (1–4). Tag only to Application (Medium/Hard) with mandatory LO tagging.
Clear explanation must accompany the correct answer, including reasoning for incorrect options.
Ensure mapping to specific chapters/subtopics with minimum four questions each.
Must be grammatically correct, conceptually aligned to NCERT content, and mapped to the sub-topic level.
Only Factual (Medium), Understanding (Easy/Medium) allowed. Avoid repetition or subparts.
Answer should be crisp and concise, ≤ 40 words, in 2–3 bullet points.
Framing must be correct, based on NCERT, and aligned to chapter/sub-topic/sub-sub-topic.
Understanding (Easy/Medium/Hard), Application (Medium/Hard). Only one question; no subparts allowed.
Answer ≤ 60 words, in 3–5 bullet points, and must align with NCERT.
Based on grade content cell and learning outcomes. Must align with Bloom’s levels: Understanding (M/H), Application (M/H).
Answer ≤ 120 words, presented in 5–7 bullet points. Must follow NCERT content.
80–100 words from the same concept. Questions: 1 mark (F/U), 1 mark (U), 2 marks (U-hard/Application-M).
Reject if passage is too long, lacks focus, includes repeated concepts, or missing necessary visual aids.
Must not require knowledge beyond NCERT curriculum.
